newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers dip, other ports steady to firm.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers dip, other ports steady to firm.

text.p: ARA bunkers dipped in line with crude futures losses on Tuesday, but prices in other European ports were firmer, dealers said.

Rotterdam 380 cst traded in the region $114-$115 fob, about $1 a tonne lower than on Monday. Traders said enquiries were healthy in the morning, but, once crude began to fade, buyers decided to hold off. A major picked up the biggest deal of the day, but that only amounted to 3,000 tonnes.
"(Buyers) are seeing negative numbers for crude and they just decided to ride it out," one supplier said.
Hamburg prices were steady, despite the ARA weakness.
Traders said discounting on Monday left little room for further price cuts.
Mediterranean bunkers were generally stronger. Spanish prices, for example, were about $2 up, catching up with Monday strength elsewhere.
French ports managed reasonable business after closure for a public holiday on Monday.
Fujairah bunkers held at year-high levels of around $116 fob. Unfortunately for suppliers, business was nowhere near year-high levels.
